nodes.summary: Bayesian inference and nonparametric priors: the Dirichlet process and stick-breaking, Pólya and Blackwell–MacQueen urns, Ferguson conjugacy, and posterior computations. Parametric conjugate models, Bayesian linear regression, expectation–maximization, mean-field variational inference, and Monte Carlo and Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling are under Bayesian inference and sampling in Machine learning. The two-groups…
nodes.title: Bayesian statistics

nodes.summary: Galton–Watson processes, extinction probabilities, total progeny and the hitting-time theorem, and linear birth–death processes.
nodes.title: Branching processes

nodes.summary: Convergence in law of normalized sums and their error terms: central limit theorems (Lindeberg–Feller, lacunary and infinite-variance variants), Berry–Esseen bounds and constants, global and local de Moivre–Laplace theorems, Edgeworth expansions, Donsker's invariance principle, and Poisson limit theorems for binomial and urn models.
nodes.title: Central limit theorems and Poisson approximation

nodes.summary: Characteristic functions, probability generating functions and positive-definite functions (Bochner), Taylor bounds for characteristic functions, lattice support, Lévy's continuity theorem and Cramér's decomposition theorem for the normal law.
nodes.title: Characteristic functions and generating functions

nodes.summary: Non-asymptotic tail and moment bounds: Hoeffding, McDiarmid, Efron–Stein, Khintchine and Paley–Zygmund inequalities, sampling without replacement, sub-Gaussian convex comparison, and hypercontractivity (Bonami–Beckner, p-biased two-point inequalities) on the discrete cube.
nodes.title: Concentration inequalities

nodes.summary: Weak convergence and convergence in probability, tightness and Prokhorov's theorem, Helly selection, Skorokhod representation, the continuous mapping theorem, the Cramér–Wold device and total variation distance; specific limit laws go to the limit-theorem fields.
nodes.title: Convergence of probability measures

nodes.summary: Inequalities comparing probabilities of monotone or disjointly occurring events under product measures, and stochastic orderings and monotone couplings of measures.
nodes.title: Correlation inequalities and stochastic domination

nodes.summary: Named discrete and continuous laws and their moments, densities, mass functions and tails (binomial, Poisson-binomial, hypergeometric, negative binomial, beta, gamma, exponential, chi-square, Dirichlet, multivariate Gaussian and Gaussian conditioning, Gaussian orthant probabilities), expectation under a probability mass function, joint laws, distribution functions, quantiles and medians; sampling laws used in tests…
nodes.title: Probability distributions

nodes.summary: Construction of probability measures and processes (Kolmogorov extension, measures from Stieltjes functions), independence, conditional expectation and regular conditional distributions, exchangeability and de Finetti's theorem, and zero–one laws for sequences (Hewitt–Savage); zero–one laws for continuous processes go to Brownian motion and stochastic calculus, tail sigma-algebras of random walks to Random walks.
nodes.title: Foundations of probability

nodes.summary: Probability in high dimension and on geometric objects: log-concave and uniform convex-body laws, isotropic constants, the KLS and thin-shell conjectures and their bounds, random matrices (singularity of Bernoulli matrices, Tracy–Widom limits), random Euclidean optimization (Beardwood–Halton–Hammersley), and suprema of selector and positive empirical processes (Park–Pham theorems).
nodes.title: High-dimensional and geometric probability

nodes.summary: Tests and their validity and power: Neyman–Pearson, likelihood-ratio, score and Wald tests, monotone likelihood ratio, exact conditional tests (Fisher, Hardy–Weinberg), rank tests and ROC area (Mann–Whitney), permutation p-values, multiple testing (familywise error control by Bonferroni, Holm and closed testing; false discovery rate control by Benjamini–Hochberg; and the two-groups model with local and tail-area…
nodes.title: Hypothesis testing

nodes.summary: Infinitely divisible and stable distributions, convolution powers, the Lévy–Khintchin representation, and regularly varying and slowly varying functions (Karamata's theorem, Potter bounds, generalized inverses) with the truncated moments and tail integrals of heavy-tailed laws.
nodes.title: Infinitely divisible laws and regular variation

nodes.summary: Large deviation principles and rate functions, Cramér's theorem and Chernoff bounds for empirical means, log-moment generating functions and the Legendre–Fenchel transform used to build them.
nodes.title: Large deviations

nodes.summary: Almost-sure behaviour of sums of independent variables: strong and weak laws of large numbers, Kolmogorov's three-series theorem and maximal inequality, truncation techniques, the law of the iterated logarithm, and the Monte Carlo variance rate of sample means.
nodes.title: Laws of large numbers and random series

nodes.summary: Multivariate normal theory and linear models: Gaussian maximum likelihood, Cochran's theorem on quadratic forms, t and F sampling laws, Gauss–Markov and generalized least squares, principal component analysis, and Gaussian graphical models. Ridge and lasso regression are under least squares, ridge and lasso regression, and probabilistic principal component analysis, with the factor-analysis marginal, under…
nodes.title: Linear models and multivariate analysis

nodes.summary: Discrete-time Markov chains (construction, path measures, finite-dimensional distributions, Chapman–Kolmogorov, Markov and strong Markov properties), finite chains, ergodicity and convergence to stationarity, mixing, reversibility and Kolmogorov's cycle criterion, and finite continuous-time Markov chains with rate matrices, semigroups and hitting times.
nodes.title: Markov chains

nodes.summary: Discrete-time martingales, sub- and supermartingales: convergence theorems (almost sure, L^p, backwards, Lévy's downward theorem), uniform integrability, Doob's maximal inequalities, orthogonality and conditional variance of increments, optional stopping in all its forms, and Wald's equations for stopped sums. Martingale measures and the fundamental theorem of asset pricing.
nodes.title: Martingales and optional stopping

nodes.summary: Distribution-free and semiparametric methods: empirical distribution functions (Glivenko–Cantelli), U-statistics, the Kaplan–Meier estimator, Cox partial likelihood and the log-rank test, and design-based causal inference with potential outcomes. Park and Pham's theorem on when the supremum of a positive empirical process over a finite family of nonnegative functions is large compared with its expectation is under…
nodes.title: Nonparametric statistics and survival analysis

nodes.summary: Bernoulli bond and site percolation: percolation probability, critical points, number and uniqueness of infinite clusters, sharpness and sharp thresholds, and crossing estimates in two dimensions.
nodes.title: Percolation

nodes.summary: Poisson processes on the line and Poisson point processes on general spaces (arrival times, counts, restriction theorem), and stationary random functions.
nodes.title: Point processes and stationary processes

nodes.summary: Spin and bond configuration spaces, Bernoulli product measures and cylinder events, Gibbs-type conditional distributions given the outside of a region, translation invariance and ergodicity, weak and monotone limits of measures on configuration space, and marginals and conditional independence for weights on finite configuration spaces.
nodes.title: Random fields on lattices

nodes.summary: Sums of i.i.d. steps as processes: the drift/oscillation dichotomy, limsup and liminf of partial sums, tail measurability of asymptotic events, the strong Markov property of i.i.d. sequences at stopping times, and ballot theorems.
nodes.title: Random walks

nodes.summary: Point estimation theory: bias, risk and mean squared error, likelihood and maximum likelihood (consistency and asymptotic normality), Fisher information and Cramér–Rao, sufficiency, factorization (Fisher–Neyman, Halmos–Savage) and Rao–Blackwell, Stein's lemma and James–Stein shrinkage, and contiguity and Le Cam's lemmas. The local asymptotic normality of the log-likelihood ratio is under local power of the…
nodes.title: Statistical estimation

nodes.summary: Continuous-time processes with continuous paths or independent increments: Kolmogorov's continuity theorem, Blumenthal-type zero–one laws, Markov property for independent-increment processes, quadratic variation, the Itô integral and Itô's formula, stochastic differential equations, the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process, and Fokker–Planck equations for diffusions.
nodes.title: Brownian motion and stochastic calculus

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
